english: [TAB]The highlight of the new Capital city was the promenade overlooking the bay of Laurus, a dazzling court held up like an offering to the mercurial gods of wind and wave. Upon this meeting place and against the wall of the palace sat the Heron Throne, looking out to the horizon. Graceful gold filigree outlines the seat, showing sea horses frolicking in waves at the bottom and the namesake birds taking flight at the top.[PARAGRAPH:1]Decius crested the stairs leading to the court. Seeing the matronly woman seated on the Heron Throne made him feel the weight of his own years, for he had first met the queen when she was in her prime and nearly as battle hardened as he had been. The years had been kind to Rhoanna, crowning her with wisdom and grace, but the greying hair and the wrinkles that accompanied her welcoming smile readily attested to the years since they had shared a crusade.[PARAGRAPH:1]He nodded courteously and addressed her as an equal. "Queen Rhoanna. I am glad to see you well."[PARAGRAPH:1]She arose, walked down the steps of the dais, and clasped his hand. "All who stood with us against Mulcarn's rebirth are ever welcome here. What tidings do you bring from the lands Myrh?"[PARAGRAPH:1]They spoke briefly of the rebuilding of the respective nations, nothing unknown to the spies both employed but making official the news of their distant realms. Decius eyed the assembled courtiers and advisors, including his own attending sorcerer and captain before broaching the reason for his visit. "I fear the peace in my lands is tenuous at best. There is a dark taint spreading from the coast deep into the heart, one resistant to my attempts at infiltration or investigation."[PARAGRAPH:1]Rhoanna frowned. "The overlords."[PARAGRAPH:1]"Yes. Once again I see an empire riven by the sign of the Octopus. Gods know I will never see eye to eye with the Bannor, but their dim view of this cult was not wrong. Whole towns have fallen asleep for weeks, wakening in madness. Abolishing their temples has only driven them underground?literally in some cases. Their connection to the oceans is obvious and I need answers from the remnants of the Lanun."[PARAGRAPH:1]"Believe me, Decius, we know of this cult. It reaches into every port town, not least these in the Meditor Sea here. It is more than a simple pagan personality cult, but for some reason the actual source of its divine power has long been difficult to determine. Falamar once received a vision from an archangel of Danalin that told of some malevolent force corrupting the god of the seas. Uncovering the source and stemming the tide of the Octopus Overlords has been his quest since the slaying of Auric. He is even now at the royal docks preparing an expedition to find an island said to be to the key to this mystery."[PARAGRAPH:1]"That's not enough, Rhoanna."[PARAGRAPH:1]"We are doing what we can."[PARAGRAPH:1]"All you have are empty words and deflection. We know most of Hannah's captains have sworn to Falamar. The last time I was tasked with carving out this cult I did so by burning Lanun cities."[PARAGRAPH:1]Rhoanna's eyebrows raised at his harsh tone. "Is that a threat, Decius?"[PARAGRAPH:1]"I will do what I need to do to protect my empire. I find it interesting that you take that as a threat."[PARAGRAPH:1]"We will overlook the implications of your words due to our past alliance. All I have for you now is an oath on my honor that we view this cult as our enemy and an offer of cooperation in eradicating it if you reciprocate in good faith."[PARAGRAPH:1]The sorcerer at Decius side leaned forward, whispering "I sense no deception, lord."[PARAGRAPH:1]Decius gestured angrily at his to be silent and turned from the Heron throne with a last word to Rhoanna. "The truth will come out, and my enemies will pay, as ever. It will be simpler if you prove upright, but I have precious little faith to offer." Rhoanna paced the length of the promenade and gazed out to the cloudy sea as he left.[PARAGRAPH:1]A winding staircase carved into the bluff led down from the court of Rhoanna and Falamar directly to the docks. Past the guard stations and not far from the fish markets, the streets were crowded with beggars harassing the emissaries and merchants docking at the royal isle. Decius turned aside before the docks, taking a path up to a scenic cliff that offered a small measure of privacy, waving to his sorcerer to follow. He said to him, "You spoke out of turn, Jerrell."[PARAGRAPH:1]"Apologies, lord, but you seemed distrustful of your friends. I wanted you to have the information my magics could glean from them. Surely, that is why I am here."[PARAGRAPH:1]"Partly, yes. I need to know who I can trust. Foreign kings have their own agenda, as do my vassals, as do the gods' tools. Everyone does." Decius grabbed the smaller man, lifted him over the cliff edge. Holding him over a precipitous drop, he added, "Don't they? You made me look a fool."[PARAGRAPH:1]"No more than your own paranoia did, my lord. Please, let us have this conversation rationally."[PARAGRAPH:1]"I sponsored your order so I could have a secular inquisition should I need it. But I wonder how strictly you work against my enemies."[PARAGRAPH:1]As discreetly as possible Jerrell pulled on the aether, gathering power. "Lord, let me request again, set me back on the ground unharmed."[PARAGRAPH:1]Decius did so. "Just as I thought. You turn your power on me at a moment's chance, faithless dog."[PARAGRAPH:1]The sorcerer bent over, panting. "Only in self-defense. When you come to your senses we can ignore this rashness."[PARAGRAPH:1]"You have perverted my senses with your charms, traitor. Much as I wish to strike you down here and now for that affront, I just can't bring myself to. I am compelled to do you no direct harm. The most I can do is refrain from waving at that mercenary I hired to wait up the path."[PARAGRAPH:1]"What?" Decius stepped back and a crossbow bolt buried itself in the sorcerer's chest. Decius shook his head sharply and kicked the man into the bay.[PARAGRAPH:1]The sergeant of the Guild of the Nine slung his crossbow and came up to Decius. "You did not give the signal, lord. As you said, this meant the wizard was to die."[PARAGRAPH:1]"Thank you, Rone. I think we need to talk about expanding our contract." He sighed wearily. "My lands have need of a purge."[NEWLINE][PARAGRAPH:1]Falamar pushed through the crowded wharf. His boyish charms long gone, his seasoned features nonetheless drew every female eye in the crowd even before they recognized his royal garb. This time he returned no longing gazes, intent on the foreign ship preparing to leave. Its owner was boarding now, he saw. An old soldier in search of a battleground. "Decius!" The emperor of Myrh turned. He looked at Falamar a moment, then turned his back on him, issuing orders to his Captain and a man wearing mercenary colors. Falamar was undeterred by the rudeness, striding aboard. "Decius, you've threatened my wife, the Queen, and brought violence to my streets."[PARAGRAPH:1]Decius gave the old pirate his attention, folding his arms across his chest as he said, "What of it Falamar?"[PARAGRAPH:1]"If you were my vassal instead of my ally, I'd keel haul you."[PARAGRAPH:1]"You can try to arrange that, if you'd like."[PARAGRAPH:1]"Like it? What I'd like is to help you, you arrogant, plagueboil. To have you help us. What have we done to earn your distrust?"[PARAGRAPH:1]Decius snorted. "My empire is more diverse than Kylorin's at its height. The Malakim remnants, ambitious vampires, Sheaim refugees, lost angels, Elven revolutionaries. Do you think I hold it together by trust? There is no trust on Erebus, only strength and will."[PARAGRAPH:1]"There was one who put his trust in you once, if the stories are true."[PARAGRAPH:1]Decius grabbed the collar of Falamar's coat. "More the fool, him! Death is my sword and deceit is my shield. There's naught but misery in my wake." The crew of the vessel paused their work, staring at the argument. Decius waved at them dismissively.[PARAGRAPH:1]"Is that a boast or a lament?" Falamar replied, unperturbed.[PARAGRAPH:1]Decius turned and leaned against the railing, gazing at the horizon. Falamar waited until finally he turned back. "What was it all for?"[PARAGRAPH:1]"You brought us the Nether blade, old comrade in arms, upon the bleakest battlefield I've ever seen. Were it not for that?and everything that led to that--there may be no civilization upon this world."[PARAGRAPH:1]"I fought my whole life to be in control. In the end, did I make a single choice of consequence? Every decision I made--every betrayal, every death, every show of mercy or burst of inspiration, all just so you could thrust that damned blade into Auric? We're all puppets."[PARAGRAPH:1]"That's not exactly how it went down?nevermind, I like your version." Falamar inhaled the sea breeze deeply. "Every time I step on a boat, she calls to me. The siren song of my first lover, she says ?Falamar, Falamar, away with me forever! You were not made to be a worm shackled to the dirt, dance upon the waves and be free.'" A smile played upon his lips as he gazed briefly back towards the Heron Throne looking down on them. "And yet, I always return. I get every breath of wind into my sails so I can step upon this shore and return to give counsel and succor to my wife and queen. Which is freer self? The one that heeds his whims or the one stays bound to vow made years ago?"[PARAGRAPH:1]Decius shrugged. "It'll take a greater bard than you to convince me the meaning of life is true love."[PARAGRAPH:1]"No, that's not what I'm getting at. We may be the playthings of greater beings--fine. But at the end of it all, we are what we choose to do. You are at another cross-road. Take a leap of faith, here, friend. You may lose something by trusting, but you will certainly lose everything if you descend into paranoia."[PARAGRAPH:1]Decius grit his teeth, wavering. He remembered another boat in a Lanun port, long ago, where he had faced the choice of light or dark. After a time he said "Well. Give my official apologies to Rhoanna, please. I believe I came off as more antagonistic then I had intended."[PARAGRAPH:1]Falamar smiled briefly. "I suppose I'll take that." Decius turned, and Falamar said, "Wait, that's not all. I have a clue to the Overlords. Two, actually. I think Rhoanna mentioned the Isle to you. There's something else, and I need your help. A wizard, or sorcerer, or something. Last seen in the Umbra Woods. He may be the key. I need you to find this man, this... Hemah."

[TAB]新都最引以为傲的，是那条俯瞰劳鲁斯湾的长廊——一座璀璨的殿庭，宛如献给那反复无常的风浪诸神的祭品，高高擎起。就在这处会见之所、倚着宫墙，坐落着苍鹭王座，遥望着地平线。优雅的金丝勾勒出座椅的轮廓，底部海马在浪花间嬉戏，顶端则是那与王座同名的飞鸟振翅欲起。[PARAGRAPH:1]德西乌斯登上通往殿庭的石阶。看见那位端坐苍鹭王座上的雍容妇人，令他倍感自己年岁的沉重——他初见这位女王时，她正当盛年，几乎与当年的他一样久经沙场。岁月待罗安娜不薄，为她加冕以智慧与优雅，可那渐白的鬓发、那随和煦笑意浮现的皱纹，无不昭示着自他们并肩征战以来流逝的年月。[PARAGRAPH:1]他彬彬有礼地颔首，以平等之礼向她致意。“罗安娜女王。见你安好，我很高兴。”[PARAGRAPH:1]她起身，走下御台的台阶，握住他的手。“凡是曾与我们并肩对抗穆尔卡恩复生之人，在此永远受欢迎。你从米尔之地带来了什么消息？”[PARAGRAPH:1]他们简短地谈起各自国度的重建，皆是双方密探早已知晓之事，只不过将这些遥远疆土的消息正式互通罢了。德西乌斯扫视着聚集的廷臣与顾问，包括他随行的术士与队长，才切入此行的缘由。“我担心我领地内的和平至多只是脆弱表象。有一股黑暗的污秽正从海岸向腹地深处蔓延，任凭我如何渗透探查都无从破解。”[PARAGRAPH:1]罗安娜蹙眉。“是霸主们。”[PARAGRAPH:1]“正是。我再度目睹一个帝国被那章鱼之印撕裂。诸神明鉴，我这辈子都别想与班诺尔人合得来，可他们对这邪教的鄙夷却没有错。整座整座的城镇沉睡数周，醒来时尽是疯狂。捣毁他们的神庙只是把他们逼入地下——某些情形下当真是钻进了地底。他们与海洋的关联显而易见，我需要从拉努恩的残部那里得到答案。”[PARAGRAPH:1]“相信我，德西乌斯，我们知晓这个邪教。它渗入每一座港城，尤以这片美地托海的港口为甚。它绝非一个简单的异教偶像崇拜，可出于某种缘由，它神力的真正源头长久以来难以查明。法拉玛曾从达纳林的一位大天使处得到启示，说是有某种恶毒之力正在腐蚀海洋之神。自奥里克被斩杀以来，探明源头、遏止深渊霸主的浪潮，便成了他的追寻。此刻他就在王家船坞，正筹备一次远征，去寻找一座据说是解开此谜关键的岛屿。”[PARAGRAPH:1]“这还不够，罗安娜。”[PARAGRAPH:1]“我们已在尽力而为。”[PARAGRAPH:1]“你所有的不过是空话与推诿。我们知道汉娜的船长大多已宣誓效忠法拉玛。上一次受命铲除这邪教时，我是靠焚烧拉努恩的城市办到的。”[PARAGRAPH:1]罗安娜听他语气严厉，扬起了眉。“这是威胁吗，德西乌斯？”[PARAGRAPH:1]“为保护我的帝国，该做的我都会做。你把这当作威胁，倒叫我觉得有趣。”[PARAGRAPH:1]“念在我们昔日的同盟，你话中的含意我们就不深究了。眼下我能给你的，只有以我名誉起誓：我们视这邪教为仇敌；倘若你以诚相待，我愿携手将其根除。”[PARAGRAPH:1]德西乌斯身旁的术士俯身上前，低声道：“我察觉不到任何欺瞒，大人。”[PARAGRAPH:1]德西乌斯怒气冲冲地摆手示意他噤声，转身背对苍鹭王座，向罗安娜留下最后一句话。“真相终会大白，我的仇敌终将付出代价，一如既往。你若证明自己正直，事情会简单些，可我能奉上的信任实在少得可怜。”他离去时，罗安娜在长廊上来回踱步，凝望着阴云笼罩的海面。[PARAGRAPH:1]一道盘旋的石阶凿入峭壁，自罗安娜与法拉玛的殿庭径直通向船坞。过了岗哨、离鱼市不远处，街上挤满了乞丐，纠缠着在王家岛屿靠岸的使节与商贾。德西乌斯在抵达船坞前转身，取道登上一处僻静的风景崖，挥手示意他的术士跟上。他对他说：“你方才多嘴了，杰瑞尔。”[PARAGRAPH:1]“恕罪，大人，可您似乎对您的友人心存戒备。我想让您获知我的法术能从他们身上探得的情报。这想必正是我在此的缘由。”[PARAGRAPH:1]“部分如此，没错。我需要知道我能信任谁。异国的君王有他们自己的算计，我的封臣亦然，诸神的爪牙同样如此。人人皆是。”德西乌斯一把抓住那矮小的男子，将他举过崖边。把他悬在陡峭的深渊之上，他又道：“不是吗？你让我出了丑。”[PARAGRAPH:1]“那也不过是您自己的多疑所致，大人。求您，让我们理智地把话说清楚。”[PARAGRAPH:1]“我扶植你的教团，是好让我在需要时能有一支世俗的裁判庭。可我不禁要问，你对付我的仇敌究竟有多尽心。”[PARAGRAPH:1]杰瑞尔尽可能不动声色地牵引以太，聚拢力量。“大人，容我再求一次，把我毫发无伤地放回地面。”[PARAGRAPH:1]德西乌斯照做了。“正如我所料。一有机会你便将力量转向我，你这没有信义的狗。”[PARAGRAPH:1]术士弯下腰，喘着粗气。“那只是自卫。等您清醒过来，我们可以当这鲁莽从未发生。”[PARAGRAPH:1]“你用你的魅惑扭曲了我的心智，叛徒。就凭这份冒犯，我恨不得此时此地将你击杀，可我偏偏下不了手。我被迫无法对你直接加害。我最多能做的，就是忍住不向我雇来守在小径尽头的那名佣兵挥手示意。”[PARAGRAPH:1]“什么？”德西乌斯退后一步，一支弩箭没入了术士的胸膛。德西乌斯猛地摇头，一脚把那人踢进了海湾。[PARAGRAPH:1]九人佣兵工会的军曹背起弩弓，走到德西乌斯跟前。“您没有发出信号，大人。正如您所言，这意味着那术士当死。”[PARAGRAPH:1]“谢谢你，罗内。我想我们得谈谈扩大合约的事。”他疲惫地叹了口气。“我的领地需要一场清洗。”[NEWLINE][PARAGRAPH:1]法拉玛挤过熙攘的码头。他那少年般的魅力早已不再，可即便众人尚未认出他的王室装束，他那历经风霜的面容仍引来人群中每一道女子的目光。这一次，他没有回应任何一道眷恋的凝视，一心只盯着那艘正准备启航的异国船只。他看见船主此刻正在登船。一名寻觅战场的老兵。“德西乌斯！”那位米尔的皇帝转过身来。他打量了法拉玛片刻，随即转身背对他，向他的队长和一名身着佣兵服色的男子发号施令。法拉玛不为这份无礼所动，径直登上船去。“德西乌斯，你威胁了我的妻子、我的女王，还在我的街道上兴起了暴力。”[PARAGRAPH:1]德西乌斯向这位老海盗投去注意，双臂抱于胸前，说道：“那又如何，法拉玛？”[PARAGRAPH:1]“你若是我的封臣而非盟友，我早把你拖过龙骨了。”[PARAGRAPH:1]“你若愿意，尽可以设法一试。”[PARAGRAPH:1]“愿意？我愿意的是帮你，你这自负的、烂疮似的家伙。是要你来帮我们。我们做了什么，竟惹得你如此不信任？”[PARAGRAPH:1]德西乌斯嗤笑一声。“我的帝国比全盛时期的凯洛林还要庞杂。马拉基姆的残部、野心勃勃的吸血鬼、塞安的难民、迷途的天使、精灵的革命党。你以为我是靠信任把它维系在一起的吗？在伊瑞布斯，没有信任，只有力量与意志。”[PARAGRAPH:1]“若那些传说属实，曾有一人把他的信任托付给了你。”[PARAGRAPH:1]德西乌斯揪住法拉玛外套的衣领。“他更是个傻瓜！死亡是我的剑，欺瞒是我的盾。我所过之处，唯余苦难。”船上的水手停下手中的活计，盯着这场争执。德西乌斯不屑地朝他们挥了挥手。[PARAGRAPH:1]“这是自夸，还是哀叹？”法拉玛不为所动地回道。[PARAGRAPH:1]德西乌斯转身倚在栏杆上，凝望着地平线。法拉玛静候着，直到他终于转回身来。“这一切究竟是为了什么？”[PARAGRAPH:1]“是你把冥界毒刃带给了我们，昔日的战友，在我所见过最凄凉的战场上。若非那一刃——若非那一切铺垫至此——这世上或许根本不会有任何文明。”[PARAGRAPH:1]“我这一生都在争取掌控。到头来，我可曾做过哪怕一个真正有分量的抉择？我做的每一个决定——每一次背叛、每一场死亡、每一回慈悲或灵光乍现，全都只是为了让你能把那该死的剑刺进奥里克体内？我们全是傀儡。”[PARAGRAPH:1]“事情的经过其实不完全是那样——算了，我倒喜欢你这个版本。”法拉玛深深吸入海风。“我每次踏上船，她都在召唤我。我初恋情人的海妖之歌，她唱道：‘法拉玛，法拉玛，随我永远离去吧！你生来不是被拴在泥土上的一条虫，去在浪尖起舞，去获得自由吧。’”他嘴角浮起一丝笑意，短暂回望着俯视他们的苍鹭王座。“可我，我总是归来。我扬满每一缕风入帆，好让自己能踏上这片岸，回来给我的妻子、我的女王进献谏言与慰藉。哪一个才是更自由的自我？是听从一时兴之所至的那个，还是恪守多年前所立誓言的那个？”[PARAGRAPH:1]德西乌斯耸耸肩。“想让我信服生命的意义就是真爱，得靠一个比你更高明的吟游诗人。”[PARAGRAPH:1]“不，我要说的不是那个。我们或许是更伟大存在的玩物——好吧。可归根结底，我们就是我们所选择去做的事。你正站在又一个岔路口。在此，纵身一跃，凭一份信念吧，朋友。信任或许会让你失去某样东西，可若你堕入多疑，你必将失去一切。”[PARAGRAPH:1]德西乌斯咬紧牙关，动摇了。他忆起许久以前拉努恩港中另一艘船上，他曾面临光明与黑暗的抉择。良久之后他说道：“也罢。请代我向罗安娜正式致歉。我想我表现得比本意要更咄咄逼人了些。”[PARAGRAPH:1]法拉玛短促一笑。“这我就领了。”德西乌斯转身欲走，法拉玛却道：“等等，还没完。我掌握了一条关于霸主们的线索。其实是两条。我想罗安娜向你提过那座岛。还有另一样，我需要你帮忙。一位巫师，或术士，或什么的。最后一次现身是在昏影林。他或许是关键所在。我需要你找到这个人，这个……赫玛。”

english: [TAB]Dreamers, worthless vagrants whose only use was receiving the visions of the Undertow, surrounded the chamber. Each lay in a shallow recess, and 27 thin bone needles pierced them in different places. The needles were hollow and filled with wax from whale fat and unholy religious oils, while in each a wick burned. As the wax melted, it seeped down the needle into the dreamers' blood, this was what induced the visions.[PARAGRAPH:1]Most of what they said was gibberish, nightmares and twisted memories. They repeated verses to old lullabies, held conversations with imaginary people, and talked in languages no one could recognize. But occasionally it was more than that.[PARAGRAPH:1]These dreams were always preceded by the Dreamers screaming. New Zealots always considered opening themselves up to receive the dreams directly, to speak directly with the Undertow, until they heard the screams.[PARAGRAPH:1]Then the voice came, a variety of voices but never that of the Dreamer. The message was given, the Cultists would faithfully record it and worship at the sides of the recess. The Dreamer was always mentally scarred by the contact, most were only good for 2 or 3 visions before they were replaced.[PARAGRAPH:1]But there were rules to dealing with the dreamers, they were sacred objects. Their food was specially prepared, they were kept clean and groomed and they weren't exposed to any sound or sight that could distress them, until Cinnia.[PARAGRAPH:1]Cinnia was a favored dreamer of the Undertow, having received 7 visions and all the Cultists except Koun of the Ninth Ring agreed she was fit to receive more. Her 8th vision was her last, the Undertow spoke through her in three voices. One yelled in outrage threatening a great wave would destroy the city if atonement was not met. Another spoke of the future, of a human terror that would lead and destroy men, the "Kraken of Fields". The last voice screamed in pain, it was broken and the Cultists were never able to decipher its message, for it was cut off halfway through the messages of the other two.[PARAGRAPH:1]For weeks the Cultists debated the meanings of the visions. Koun argued that Cinnia should be killed, that her sacrifice was the atonement the Undertow demanded. Each day they watched the sea, fearful of a coming wave. Then the Cultists noticed that the sea was beginning to recede, to pull away from the city. The water was gathering somewhere distant, the wave was coming.[PARAGRAPH:1]They rushed to the chamber, worshipped beside Cinnia, asked for guidance on how to appease their masters. They stayed there until one of them noticed Cinnia's stomach had expanded slightly. A sorcerer confirmed it, she was pregnant.[PARAGRAPH:1]The rest of the day was chaos. A dreamer had been befouled, and only Cultists had access to them. Under threat and coercion they found who had done it: Koun of the Ninth Ring.[PARAGRAPH:1]Koun was sacrificed at the beach and the wave never came. Cinnia was taken from the chamber and tended to. She died in childbirth, but gave birth two girls, one was stillborn, the other survived.[PARAGRAPH:1]The Cultists decided that the child was too dangerous to be kept in the temple, so she was given to a Lanun ship captain to raise. He named her Hannah the Irin, after being told she was a twin whose mother and sister died in childbirth.[PARAGRAPH:1]Hannah became as temperamental and powerful as the sea itself. She left her fathers ship at 15 and led a mutiny against her next ship's captain to take it from him. That ship, which she renamed the 'Desecrated Vessel' became feared by military and merchant ships alike. When the time for war came, pirates flocked to her flag. Unaccustomed to central rule, the Lanun follow Hannah, too afraid to do otherwise.
chinese: [TAB]梦者们——一群一文不值的流浪汉，唯一的用处便是承受暗流的幻象——环绕着这间密室。每人都躺在一处浅浅的凹龛中，二十七根细长的骨针从不同部位刺入他们体内。骨针是空心的，灌满了鲸脂炼成的蜡与不洁的宗教圣油，每根针里都燃着一根灯芯。蜡一旦熔化，便顺着骨针渗入梦者的血液，正是这唤起了幻象。[PARAGRAPH:1]他们所说的大多是胡言乱语，是噩梦与扭曲的记忆。他们反复念诵古老摇篮曲的词句，与虚构的人交谈，用无人能辨的语言呓语。可偶尔，那会是更多的东西。[PARAGRAPH:1]这些梦总以梦者的尖叫为前兆。新入门的狂信徒总想着直接敞开自己去承接梦境，直接与暗流对话——直到他们听见那尖叫。[PARAGRAPH:1]随后那声音便来了，形形色色的声音，却从不是梦者本人的。讯息一经传达，狂热祭司们便忠实地记录下来，跪在凹龛两侧膜拜。梦者总在这番接触后落下心智的创伤，大多在被替换之前只堪承受两三次幻象。[PARAGRAPH:1]可对待梦者是有规矩的，他们是神圣之物。他们的食物经过特别调制，被保持洁净、梳理整齐，绝不让他们接触任何可能令其惊扰的声响或景象——直到辛尼亚出现。[PARAGRAPH:1]辛尼亚是暗流宠爱的梦者，已承受过七次幻象，除了第九环的寇恩，所有狂热祭司都认定她适合承受更多。她的第八次幻象成了她的最后一次，暗流借她之口以三种嗓音说话。一个嗓音愤怒地咆哮，威胁说若不赎罪，一道巨浪将摧毁整座城。另一个诉说着未来，说有一个人间的恐怖将统领并毁灭众生，那“田野的海妖”。最后一个嗓音在痛苦中尖叫，它支离破碎，狂热祭司们始终无法破译它的讯息，因为它在另外两个嗓音的传述途中戛然而止。[PARAGRAPH:1]狂热祭司们为这些幻象的含义争论了数周。寇恩主张应当杀死辛尼亚，说她的献祭正是暗流所要求的赎罪。他们日复一日地注视着大海，惧怕那即将到来的巨浪。随后，狂热祭司们察觉海水开始退去，从城边抽离。海水正在某处遥远的地方聚集，巨浪将至。[PARAGRAPH:1]他们冲进密室，在辛尼亚身旁膜拜，祈求指引，好安抚他们的主人。他们守在那里，直到其中一人注意到辛尼亚的腹部微微隆起。一名术士证实了此事：她怀孕了。[PARAGRAPH:1]那一天余下的时光陷入了混乱。一名梦者遭到了玷污，而唯有狂热祭司能接近她们。在威逼与胁迫之下，他们查出了行凶者：第九环的寇恩。[PARAGRAPH:1]寇恩在海滩上被献祭，那巨浪终究没有到来。辛尼亚被从密室中带出，得到悉心照料。她死于分娩，却诞下两个女婴，一个死产，另一个活了下来。[PARAGRAPH:1]狂热祭司们判定这孩子太过危险，不宜留在神庙，于是把她交给一位拉努恩船长抚养。船长被告知她是一对双胞胎中的幸存者，母亲与姐妹皆死于分娩，便给她取名艾尔琳的汉娜。[PARAGRAPH:1]汉娜长得像大海本身一样喜怒无常、威力无穷。她十五岁便离开父亲的船，又率领一场哗变，从下一任船长手中夺走了他的船。那艘被她改名为“亵渎号”的船，令军舰与商船同样闻风丧胆。战争来临之际，海盗们纷纷聚集到她的旗下。拉努恩人不习惯中央统治，却追随汉娜，只因不敢有别的选择。

english: [TAB]The battle was fierce, but the Bannor men proved true. Turin was called up from the reserves, and he gathered his relics and poultices assuming he was needed to tend the wounded. Alas, the body they presented to him was beyond his or his god's help.[PARAGRAPH:1]"Turin..." Aethil begin, "we found it in the fire-pit. I'm sorry, my friend." The guardsman held out his hand, displaying the tiny bracelet with the Acolyte's family crest. Turin grabbed it and pushed past him, kneeling before the fire-pit. The blood of orcs and men, mingled with the melting snow soaked though his pants as he cradled the tiny skull he found there in his hands.[PARAGRAPH:1]"My Jessua..." he murmured. The hope had been small, but it had been, and now it died at the sight of his daughter's ashes.[PARAGRAPH:1]"At least these Orcs will take no more sacrifices," Aethil said, wiping his saber and surveying the wasted camp. "Though we're likely to find another camp here as soon as we turn our back."[PARAGRAPH:1]"Lieutenant!" A warrior approached them, a bundle in his arms. "This one's still alive."[PARAGRAPH:1]Aethil grabbed the Orc child by the leg, holding it up to examine as the wrappings fell to the trampled earth. "A girl. Damned ugly, but definitely a girl. Turin, take it. Kill it, you'll feel better."[PARAGRAPH:1]Turin took the child from his friend, cradling it in his arms as he had his own. "This girl did not kill my own. No justice is served by her death."[PARAGRAPH:1]"It is a corruption, a blight. You'll be saving someone else's child from the ravages of the beasts she'll spawn."[PARAGRAPH:1]"Aethil, she's a baby!"[PARAGRAPH:1]"Fine, leave it here to die by the wind and the wolves. Or were you planning on raising it yourself?"[PARAGRAPH:1]The priest had already wrapped the child his own fur cloak. "I shall, then Aethil. And we'll see how she takes to civilization. If law and goodness can be taught, maybe our relentless war could end."[PARAGRAPH:2]"Confessor Turin! Come in, come in. I was so sorry to hear about your wife."[PARAGRAPH:1]Turin ran a hand through his hair and sighed. "Yes. We had dreamed of living to see the end of Winter together... I guess she gets to see green pastures... before I do." Turin let the Adept lead him to a chair by the fireplace, and they sat for a moment in silence. "How go your studies, Pharsalus?"[PARAGRAPH:1]"Good news at last. Official sanction from Torrolerial and Sabathiel himself, so they say. We may continue our studies on the mana we have uncovered as long as it aids the war and contributes to the land's law and peace."[PARAGRAPH:1]"Well, then, I have a favor to ask you. My.... The Orc child-"[PARAGRAPH:1]"Yes, how is she?"[PARAGRAPH:1]"I fear I was overly optimistic. She has grown demanding and selfish, barely able to toddle around, just learning our speech, and it's ‘no' this and ‘no' that. It seems her chaotic nature asserts herself. With the passing of my wife, it is becoming so difficult to raise her, between that and my duties. But I'd hate to have to send her out."[PARAGRAPH:1]"Jessua... she died at what age?"[PARAGRAPH:1]"She'd been just weaned when they took her. What are you implying?"[PARAGRAPH:1]"Simply that perhaps you don't have the experience to judge this Orc child. Many children are-"[PARAGRAPH:1]"No. My sweet Jessua would not do the things this child does!"[PARAGRAPH:1]"Very well, my friend, what is the favor?"[PARAGRAPH:1]"I heard rumors of a spell you have uncovered. One that can touch minds and bind loyalties. Cast this on my child."[PARAGRAPH:1]Pharsalus sighed. "I should protest that it is extremely experimental, but I know better than to try to dissuade you. I could do it here and now, if you had a clump of hair or some other part of her."[PARAGRAPH:1]Turin pulled out a small fang and held it up. "She just lost a tooth."[PARAGRAPH:1]The Adept took it and walked to the next room, bare of furniture except for shelves of reagents and a perfectly round fire-pit carved out of the stone floor. He picked a few ingredients out, added the tooth, and started the fire. In went an item now and then as he intoned words, some in the common language, some in a more ancient tongue, ending with, "Qualum en noctum et solum nivum sheelba!"[PARAGRAPH:1]Turin watched from the doorway, uncertain that the ritual was over until Pharsalus turned to him. "It is done. The spell will be strengthened whenever you repeat that last word in her presence."[PARAGRAPH:1]"Sheelba."[PARAGRAPH:1]"Yes. It is from her native tongue. Forsaken. ‘Whether in night or day, never to be forsaken.'"[PARAGRAPH:1]"Thank you my friend. I shudder to think what would become of me if I raised a wild Orc in the heart of the Tor Elyr."[PARAGRAPH:2]Wild celebration was occurring throughout the civilized world, and the home of the High Priest of Tor Elyr was no exception. "To those that didn't make it to this day," Turin toasted his friends with the finest wine. The windows had been thrown wide open, letting in not the chill winds of winter but the gentle breezes of spring, at last. The city guard Captain chugged his down in one swig.[PARAGRAPH:1]"More! Might as well finish this vintage Turin, the coming harvest is sure to make a much better wine."[PARAGRAPH:1]"Indeed, my friend." Turin rose to satisfy Aethil's request.[PARAGRAPH:1]"Sit, sit. Why do you bother to get up when you have this Orc here to do your chores?"[PARAGRAPH:1]"It isn't..." Turin sat. "Sheelba, get some more wine for our friend."[PARAGRAPH:1]"Yes father." As she left, Turin drained his own glass, adding it to the pile of empties.[PARAGRAPH:1]"You let her call you that? ‘Father!'" Aethil spat the word. "You're not her father. I know, I probably killed him myself, 12, 13 years ago was it now?"[PARAGRAPH:1]"Aethil! Please, this is a happy time," Pharsalus interrupted, spilling wine down the front of his robes.[PARAGRAPH:1]"I suppose you dress her up in Kiradia's clothing? Call her little Sheeba Jessua Stonelaw do you? It's vulgar, I tell you."[PARAGRAPH:1]"It isn't... she's not... She's not my daughter, Aethil, I know that. Keeping her here amuses me, alright? Better than out pillaging isn't it?" Turin averted his gaze from his friend's eyes when he said it.[PARAGRAPH:1]"It is if she ever manages to bring back that wine." Aethil got up and staggered towards that kitchen. "Girl! The men are thirsty here!" Turin and Pharsalus followed him. They found the wine sitting on the kitchen counter and the back door wide open. A quick search showed the girl missing.[PARAGRAPH:1]"Where is she?" Turin asked.[PARAGRAPH:1]"I think... I think she heard us talking, Turin," Pharsalus said. "I think she heard you and ran off..."[PARAGRAPH:1]"She can't leave me! She's all I have!" He turned to the mage. "Pharsalus, I said your word every day, so much so she thought it was her name! Where's your Loyalty spell now?"[PARAGRAPH:1]"My what? You mean... way back then? That was ten years ago! I was but an adept then, and I told you the spell was still experimental!"[PARAGRAPH:1]"So it wore off?"[PARAGRAPH:1]"No, it never took effect. I had the reagents wrong. I thought I told you..."[PARAGRAPH:1]"Of course it took effect! From that day on she never left my side! She became the most true and loyal daughter I'd ever seen."[PARAGRAPH:1]Aethil saw that anguish in his friend's eyes, and it momentarily overcame his hate for the people he had fought against all his life. "Turin, don't you see? See wasn't loyal because she was ensorcelled! She grew up! She became your daughter once you began treating her like she was going to stay with you, rather than always looking for some glimmer of rebellion in her."[PARAGRAPH:1]The confessor fell to his knees, grasping his graying hair. "Good gods, what have I done?"[PARAGRAPH:2]She ran out of the village, tearing away the trappings of civilization. Words escaped her, and she let out a roar, rushing through the dense jungle. She was nearly naked by the time he grabbed her.[PARAGRAPH:1]"Gotcha! Hey, you aren't human," the huge Orc said.[PARAGRAPH:1]"No, no I'm not, am I?" Sheelba shook herself free. "I'm not, and he's not my father, and they mean nothing to me, they can burn they can all burn!" She beat the chest of the Orc in front of her with each word. Out of breath, she finally collapsed at his feet. He lifted her up.[PARAGRAPH:1]"I am Rantine of the Ember Clans. Who are you?"[PARAGRAPH:1]"I am Sheeba."[PARAGRAPH:1]"Come, Sheelba, I will take you home."

[TAB]那场战斗惨烈，可班诺尔的将士证明了自己的忠勇。图林从后备队中被征召上来，他收拾好圣物与药膏，只当是需要他去照料伤者。可叹，他们抬到他面前的那具躯体，已非他或他的神所能救治。[PARAGRAPH:1]“图林……”艾希尔开口道，“我们在火坑里找到了它。我很遗憾，我的朋友。”那名护卫伸出手，掌心托着一只刻有秩序使者家族纹章的小手镯。图林一把抓过手镯，从他身边挤过去，跪倒在火坑前。兽人与人类的鲜血混着融雪，浸透了他的裤子，他把在那里找到的一具小小的头骨捧在手中。[PARAGRAPH:1]“我的洁苏娃……”他喃喃道。希望本就渺茫，可它毕竟曾存在过，而如今，在他女儿的骨灰面前，它熄灭了。[PARAGRAPH:1]“至少这些兽人再也夺不走别的祭品了，”艾希尔说着，擦拭着他的马刀，环视着这座被毁的营地。“不过我们一转身，只怕这儿转眼又会冒出另一座营地。”[PARAGRAPH:1]“中尉！”一名战士走近他们，臂弯里抱着一个襁褓。“这个还活着。”[PARAGRAPH:1]艾希尔抓住那兽人幼崽的腿，把它提起来查看，襁褓褪落到被踩烂的泥地上。“是个女的。丑得要命，可确实是个女的。图林，接着。杀了它，你会好受些。”[PARAGRAPH:1]图林从友人手中接过孩子，像抱自己的孩子那样把它搂在怀里。“这女孩没有杀我的孩子。杀了她，也讨不回半分公道。”[PARAGRAPH:1]“它是个祸害，是个瘟疫。你杀了它，就是把别人家的孩子从她将来孳生的那些畜生的蹂躏中救出来。”[PARAGRAPH:1]“艾希尔，她只是个婴儿！”[PARAGRAPH:1]“好吧，那就把它扔在这儿，让风和狼要了它的命。要不然你打算自己把它养大？”[PARAGRAPH:1]祭司已经用自己的毛皮斗篷把孩子裹了起来。“那我就养，艾希尔。我们倒要看看她如何适应文明。倘若律法与善良能够教化，或许我们这场无休无止的战争终能了结。”[PARAGRAPH:2]“忏悔祭司图林！请进，请进。听说尊夫人的事，我深感痛惜。”[PARAGRAPH:1]图林用手抚过头发，叹了口气。“是啊。我们曾梦想一同活到寒冬终结之日……我想，她能比我先看到那片青绿的牧野了。”图林任由那术士领他到壁炉旁的椅子上坐下，二人默然相对片刻。“你的钻研进展如何，法尔萨卢斯？”[PARAGRAPH:1]“总算有好消息了。据说得到了托罗勒里亚尔乃至萨巴曦尔本人的正式恩准。只要有助于战事、有益于国土的律法与安宁，我们便可继续研究我们发掘出的能量。”[PARAGRAPH:1]“那好，我有一事相求。我的……那个兽人孩子——”[PARAGRAPH:1]“对了，她如何了？”[PARAGRAPH:1]“我怕是当初过于乐观了。她变得贪得无厌、自私自利，才刚学会蹒跚走路，才刚学会我们的话，就满口这个‘不要’、那个‘不要’。看来她那混沌的本性正在显露。妻子去世后，加上我的职责在身，养育她越来越是艰难。可我又不忍心把她送走。”[PARAGRAPH:1]“洁苏娃……她过世时多大？”[PARAGRAPH:1]“他们掳走她时，她才刚断奶。你这是什么意思？”[PARAGRAPH:1]“只是说，或许你并没有足够的经验来评判这个兽人孩子。许多孩子都是——”[PARAGRAPH:1]“不。我温柔的洁苏娃绝不会做这孩子做的那些事！”[PARAGRAPH:1]“好吧，我的朋友，你要求我帮的是什么？”[PARAGRAPH:1]“我听到传言，说你发掘出了一道咒法。一道能触及心灵、缚定忠诚的咒法。把它施在我的孩子身上。”[PARAGRAPH:1]法尔萨卢斯叹了口气。“我本该抗议说它还极不成熟，可我深知劝你不动。你若有她的一绺头发或身上别的什么，我此刻就能施法。”[PARAGRAPH:1]图林掏出一颗小小的獠牙，举了起来。“她刚掉了一颗牙。”[PARAGRAPH:1]术士接过牙，走进隔壁房间。那房间空无家具，只有几排摆着药剂的架子，以及在石地板上凿出的一处滚圆的火坑。他挑出几样材料，添入那颗牙，燃起火来。他一边念诵咒语，时而添入一样东西，有些是通用的语言，有些则是更为古老的言辞，末了念道：“Qualum en noctum et solum nivum english: [TAB]The Age of Ice was a paradise compared to what I endured. As men huddled in frozen caves, and the Bannor raced across the plains of ash in Agares hell I was held underneath the fractured surface of Camulos's hell.[PARAGRAPH:1]Camulos is the god of war, and his hell is the proving ground for new demons. Here they learn the arts of chaotic battle in the unending wars that rage across its surface. The souls, once moral, become desensitized to feeling and inflicting pain. Then they begin to delight in it, cruelly destroying anyone weaker than them across the volcanic terrain.[PARAGRAPH:1]Beneath the wars, in pits regularly opened or consumed by the violent earthquakes that shake the world, are the vast prisons where the victims of war are kept. I had suffered through the mire of Mulcarn, passed the trials of Mammon's great city but I was a quick victim to violence of this realm.[PARAGRAPH:1]Torturers usually want something from their victims, secrets, cooperation or conversion. But here they subjected us to anguish only to enjoy our suffering. And in a world without the escape of death, there was no hope of an end to the torment. You bleed and scream for centuries.[PARAGRAPH:1]The eruptions occasionally open new tunnels in the prisons, collapsing walls allow the imprisoned to flee to the world's surface and escape their torment for a time.[PARAGRAPH:1]After one of these I fled into wastes, where the sand cut through exposed flesh like small shards of glass. I huddled beneath the hide of a pit beast and gripped one of the back spikes from the beast as a crude weapon. My magic failed me in hell. I traced a rune in the sand, a fire sign with broken bindings and willed it alive. A faint flame flickered within it. When I was alive I could have summoned torrents of fire out of the rune, I could have assaulted a city with it. Now it only flickered weakly.[PARAGRAPH:1]Howls interrupted my concentration. Demons avoided battles in the wastes, but hunters lead by hellhounds would come through looking for those, like myself, that sought refuge here. I brushed away the rune and started deeper into the wastes.[PARAGRAPH:1]By they were faster than I was and the hound could smell me. They didn't follow scent like moral dogs, they could smell fear and there was no escaping them. As I scrambled across another ridge a darkened figure rushed at me, spear in hand. He was emaciated, weak, and I easily knocked the spear aside.[PARAGRAPH:1]I pulled the man to the ground, he was trembling, and whispered into his ear.[PARAGRAPH:1]"You will be okay" I lied, "I won't hurt you, but we have to kill the hound that is coming for us."[PARAGRAPH:1]He didn't speak, but his eyes stared into my face, trying to find some compassion. It was a rare commodity in this world.[PARAGRAPH:1]"Hide under the ridge.” I ordered, pushing him into position. "When the hound comes be ready with your spear and we will attack it together."[PARAGRAPH:1]He hid under the ridge and I slipped away. A few minutes later the hound stopped howling, it was close.[PARAGRAPH:1]The hound was drawn to the figures fear as I had suspected. I watched as it walked up to the top of the ridge and stopped to sniff and listen. Even I could sense the man's fear, I knew it was like a beacon to the hound. In one smooth movement the hound leapt off the ridge and in front of the man, he called for my help as he braced his spear.[PARAGRAPH:1]I ignored him as the hound attacked, tearing quickly into the man. I wasn't interested in the hound or the man. I waited until I saw him. A black figure wreathed in violet flames, the hunter following after the hound. As he passed I leapt out, shoving the spike into the hunters neck.[PARAGRAPH:1]The sound he made was a mix of pleasure and pain, the scream of a sadist in the ecstasy of mutilation. He was stronger than I suspected, and the spike jutting from his neck didn't slow him at all. He lifted one arm and tossed me aside. I rolled and came to my feet to see him ready for his next attack. The hound dragged the body of the man back towards us, and the deep red eyes of the rest of the hellhound pack came out of the wastes. There was at least a dozen of them. The hunter didn't bother removing the spike from his neck.[PARAGRAPH:1]A crow passed over us. Seeing it in hell was as unusual as seeing a demon flying by in Erebus. But the effect on the hunter and his hounds was immediate. They fled in all directions, even leaving the prize of the wizened man behind.[PARAGRAPH:1]The crow landed. It was large for a crow but not unnaturally so. It clawed at the ground and hopped about ignoring me. I had lost the spike and without any sort of weapon I knew I was helpless. Remembering the man's spear I started to slip by, to avoid the crow and get to base of the ridge where the hellhound and the man fought.[PARAGRAPH:1]Then I noticed what the crow had scratched. It was a fire rune with broken bindings. The crow looked at me for the first time.[PARAGRAPH:1]It was exactly like the rune I had made, perfectly formed. I walked closer and the crow crooked its head watching me. I took a breath and reached out to the rune and I immediately felt the power well up inside of me. Balefire flooded out of the rune in great wild gouts. It flowed out between the hills of the wastes, down along the ridge and all around me. At the rune itself it reached up like a fountain of yellow fire, a bright finger reaching into the sky.[PARAGRAPH:1]This was the power I once had. Let the hunters come, let them bring their packs of hellhounds, the torturers and the war machines of hell. I will purge this horrific world.[PARAGRAPH:1]The crow was gone. In its place, floating weightless just above the ground was a beautiful woman wearing purple robes. The robes floated about her in a maze of folds that hid her and offered tantalizing glimpses of her perfect pale skin. Half of an obsidian mask covered the left side of her face. On the right her lips were full and red, her eyes matched the deep purple of her robes.[PARAGRAPH:1]"To long have you dwelled in these lands."[PARAGRAPH:1]The fire collapsed back into the rune. I felt the power slip from me and I gasped and fell to my knees in an effort to keep hold of it. But it was pulled from me and I was weak again. I screamed, it was as cruel as anything I had suffered here.[PARAGRAPH:1]"Give it back." I threatened, realizing that I didn't have a weapon.[PARAGRAPH:1]Her eyes narrowed dangerously. Her body twisted and she expanded, or the world shrank, until she filled the sky and her robes surrounded me.[PARAGRAPH:1]"I am Ceridwen" she said and the ground rumbled with her voice, "and I can drop you into worlds far worse than this one. If you wish to be free you will worship me, for I am the only one who can break your chains."[PARAGRAPH:1]And I fell to the ground and worshipped her.[NEWLINE][PARAGRAPH:1]I had forgotten how beautiful creation was, or I had paid little attention. The island I walked across was ripe and lush. There were no land animals on it, just brightly colored birds that cried and fluttered away in annoyance as I walked by.[PARAGRAPH:1]A vast well stood at the center of the island. Far enough across that a galleon could have been dropped down it and it was deeper than the world. The rocks around it appeared to be old granite, but I knew that rock was the foundation of creation and was much stronger than simple granite. There were no animals here.[PARAGRAPH:1]I began walking around the well. Every few feet I stopped to trace a rune on the rock. Though it seemed a minor effect, and I was more powerful than I had ever been in life, it took all of my willpower to mar the rock. Between runes I rested and went over Ceridwen's demands, making sure each step was done exactly as she described.[PARAGRAPH:1]By the time I had walked the entire way around it was well into the night. I stood on the last rock ready to trace the final rune. But before that I drew silver letters on a black cloth, cast and then placed the cloth over my eyes. Through it I saw the spirit world. Even now spirits of the dead walked across the island and threw themselves into the well, passing from this world to the world beyond.[PARAGRAPH:1]Then I completed the final rune. In a screeching that brought back painful memories of Camulos's hell the rock began to move together. The well began to close.[PARAGRAPH:1]Confused spirits rushed toward the well, seeing their afterlife being stolen from them and from within the well I heard the sound of feathers. A cold wind came up out of the well and I saw a figure flying up at me from the wells depths. A woman with a cloth over her eyes much as mine, and ragged bands woven around her arms and into a tattered dress. She had dark wings and pale ivory skin. She was like moonlight filtered through a canopy of branches.[PARAGRAPH:1]But she was not fast enough. I reached out and pulled all of the surrounding spirits towards me, funneling them all into the final rune that was being sketched over the closing rocks surface. A barrier held fast, a great mirror that would send those who tried to pass through it back, a transformation that would bind the spirits that passed through it into unholy forms.[PARAGRAPH:1]The spirits powered the rune, they were trapped within it. They howled and fought the rune but they could not escape.[PARAGRAPH:1]To test the spell I walked to a nearby apple tree, since the birds didn't come this close to the well its fruit was untouched. But it was early in the year and it only had tiny green apples hanging from its branches.[PARAGRAPH:1]I traced a rune of withering on its trunk and the tree immediately shriveled and died. The tiny apples fell from the branches as the branches thinned and weakened. For a moment nothing happened, and then the tree filled out again. Not to its original height, as it remained dark and warped by the spell, but it was not completely dead. On its branches new small fruit blossomed, but this time they were a deep brownish red and they beat slowly.[PARAGRAPH:1]My mission had begun. My deal with Ceridwen, to bring Armageddon to creation starts here. If I fail I will return to the eternal prison of hell, and even if it means destroying the world I will never again suffer hells torments.

[TAB]与我所承受的相比，冰封纪元简直是天堂。当人类蜷缩在冰封的洞穴中，当班诺尔人在阿加雷斯地狱的灰烬平原上疾驰时，我被囚在卡姆罗斯地狱那龟裂地表之下。[PARAGRAPH:1]卡姆罗斯是战争之神，他的地狱是新生恶魔的试炼场。在这里，他们于席卷地表、永无止息的战争中学习混沌搏杀之术。那些一度尚有德性的灵魂，渐渐对施加与承受痛苦变得麻木。而后他们开始以此为乐，在这火山遍布的地界上，残忍地摧毁一切比自己弱小的存在。[PARAGRAPH:1]在这些战争之下，在那被撼动世界的剧烈地震反复掘开或吞没的深坑里，是关押战争俘虏的浩大牢狱。我曾熬过穆尔卡恩的泥沼，通过了玛门大城的种种考验，可在这一界的暴虐面前，我转眼便沦为牺牲品。[PARAGRAPH:1]施刑者通常想从受害者身上得到什么——秘密、合作或皈依。可在这里，他们令我们遭受苦楚，只为享受我们的痛苦。而在一个没有死亡可供逃遁的世界里，这折磨没有半分终结的希望。你流血、你尖叫，一叫便是数百年。[PARAGRAPH:1]喷发偶尔会在牢狱中掘开新的通道，坍塌的墙壁让被囚者得以逃向世界的表面，暂且逃离他们的折磨。[PARAGRAPH:1]一次喷发之后，我逃入了荒野，那里的沙砾如小小的玻璃碎片般割裂裸露的皮肉。我蜷在一头深坑巨兽的兽皮下，攥着从那畜生背上拔下的一根尖刺当作简陋的武器。在地狱里，我的魔法失灵了。我在沙上画下一道符文，一个带着断裂束缚的火之印记，并意念令它苏醒。一星微弱的火焰在其中闪烁。生前的我本可从这符文中召唤出滔天的烈焰，本可用它攻打一座城池。而如今它只是虚弱地闪烁。[PARAGRAPH:1]嚎叫打断了我的凝神。恶魔们避开荒野中的战斗，可由地狱犬引路的猎手会前来搜寻像我这样在此寻求庇护之人。我抹去符文，向荒野更深处走去。[PARAGRAPH:1]可它们比我快，那猎犬能嗅到我。它们不像凡间的犬那样循着气味，它们能嗅到恐惧，而恐惧是无从遮掩的。我攀过又一道山脊时，一个昏暗的身影持矛朝我扑来。他形容枯槁、虚弱不堪，我轻易便格开了那杆矛。[PARAGRAPH:1]我把那人拽倒在地，他浑身颤抖，我凑到他耳边低语。[PARAGRAPH:1]“你不会有事的，”我撒了谎，“我不会伤害你，可我们必须杀死那头正朝我们扑来的猎犬。”[PARAGRAPH:1]他没有说话，只是双眼直勾勾地凝视着我的脸，试图从中找到一丝怜悯。在这个世界，怜悯是稀罕之物。[PARAGRAPH:1]“藏到山脊下面去。”我命令道，把他推到位置上。“猎犬来时，握紧你的矛准备好，我们一起攻击它。”[PARAGRAPH:1]他藏到山脊下，我则悄然溜走。几分钟后，猎犬停止了嚎叫，它近了。[PARAGRAPH:1]正如我所料，猎犬被那身影的恐惧引了过来。我注视着它走上山脊顶端，停下来嗅探、聆听。连我都能感觉到那人的恐惧，我知道那对猎犬而言如同一座灯塔。猎犬一个利落的动作跃下山脊，落在那人面前，他一边支起长矛，一边呼喊我来相助。[PARAGRAPH:1]猎犬扑上去、飞快撕咬那人时，我不予理会。我对猎犬和那人都不感兴趣。我等待着，直到我看见他——一个裹在紫罗兰色火焰中的黑色身影，跟在猎犬身后的猎手。他经过时，我猛地跃出，将那根尖刺捅进猎手的脖颈。[PARAGRAPH:1]他发出的声响混杂着愉悦与痛苦，是一个虐待狂在残害狂喜中的尖叫。他比我料想的更强壮，脖子上戳出的尖刺丝毫不曾拖慢他。他抬起一臂，把我甩到一旁。我翻滚着重新站起，只见他已准备好下一击。猎犬把那人的尸体拖回我们身边，其余地狱犬群那一双双深红的眼睛也从荒野中现身。它们至少有十几头。那猎手懒得去拔脖子上的尖刺。[PARAGRAPH:1]一只乌鸦从我们头顶飞过。在地狱见到乌鸦，如同在伊瑞布斯见到一头恶魔飞掠而过一般罕见。可它对那猎手和他的猎犬产生的效果却是立竿见影。它们四散奔逃，甚至丢下了那枯槁男子这份猎物。[PARAGRAPH:1]乌鸦落了下来。对一只乌鸦而言它算是大的，却也不至于大得反常。它在地上抓挠、蹦跳，对我不理不睬。我丢了那尖刺，手无寸铁，我知道自己已无力自保。想起那人的长矛，我开始悄悄溜过去，绕开乌鸦，去往山脊脚下猎犬与那人厮杀之处。[PARAGRAPH:1]随后我注意到了乌鸦抓挠出的东西。那是一道带着断裂束缚的火之符文。乌鸦第一次看向了我。[PARAGRAPH:1]它与我画的那道符文一模一样，形制完美。我走近些，乌鸦歪着头注视着我。我吸了一口气，伸手触向那符文，力量立刻在我体内涌起。厄焰从符文中如狂野的洪流般奔涌而出。它在荒野的山丘间流淌，顺着山脊而下，环绕在我周身。在符文所在之处，它如一泓黄色火焰的喷泉般拔起，一根明亮的手指伸向天空。[PARAGRAPH:1]这正是我曾拥有的力量。让猎手们来吧，让他们带上成群的地狱犬、施刑者与地狱的战争机器来吧。我要涤荡这恐怖的世界。[PARAGRAPH:1]乌鸦不见了。取而代之的，是一位身着紫袍、离地悬浮的绝美女子。袍子在她周身飘拂，层叠如迷宫般的褶皱既遮蔽着她，又撩人地泄露出她那无瑕苍白肌肤的惊鸿一瞥。半张黑曜石面具遮住了她左侧的脸。右侧，她的双唇丰润红艳，双眼与她那身袍子一般是深邃的紫。[PARAGRAPH:1]“你在这片土地上盘桓得太久了。”[PARAGRAPH:1]火焰塌缩回符文之中。我感到那力量从我体内滑走，我倒抽一口气，跪倒在地，竭力想抓住它。可它被从我身上抽离，我又变得虚弱了。我尖叫起来，那痛苦如同我在此承受过的一切一样残酷。[PARAGRAPH:1]“把它还给我。”我威胁道，却意识到自己手无寸铁。[PARAGRAPH:1]她双眼危险地眯起。她的身躯扭曲、膨胀，又或是世界缩小了，直到她充满整片天空，她的袍子将我笼罩其中。[PARAGRAPH:1]“我是刻里德温，”她说，大地随她的声音隆隆震颤，“我能把你抛入远比此地更糟的世界。你若想获得自由，便要膜拜我，因为唯有我能斩断你的锁链。”[PARAGRAPH:1]于是我伏倒在地，膜拜了她。[NEWLINE][PARAGRAPH:1]我已忘了造物曾是何等瑰丽，又或是我从未曾留心。我脚下行走的这座岛屿丰饶而葱郁。岛上没有陆地走兽，只有色彩斑斓的飞鸟，在我走过时惊叫着、扑棱着翅膀恼怒地飞开。[PARAGRAPH:1]一口浩大的井矗立在岛屿中央。它宽得足以将一艘大帆船投入其中，深得超过了这个世界。井周的岩石看似古老的花岗岩，可我知道那岩石是造物的根基，远比寻常的花岗岩坚硬得多。这里没有任何走兽。[PARAGRAPH:1]我开始绕着井行走。每隔几步我便停下，在岩石上刻画一道符文。这看似微不足道的举动，纵然我已比生前任何时候都更强大，却仍需耗尽我全部的意志才能在岩石上留下痕迹。刻画符文的间隙，我歇息片刻，反复思量刻里德温的要求，确保每一步都严格照她所述完成。[PARAGRAPH:1]待我绕完整整一圈，已是深夜。我站在最后一块岩石上，准备刻下最后一道符文。可在此之前，我在一块黑布上以银色写下字符，念咒之后将黑布覆于双眼之上。透过它，我看见了灵界。即便此刻，亡者的魂灵仍在岛上游走，将自己投入井中，从这个世界通往彼岸的世界。[PARAGRAPH:1]随后我刻完了最后一道符文。在一阵勾起卡姆罗斯地狱痛苦记忆的尖啸中，岩石开始相互合拢。井开始闭合。[PARAGRAPH:1]困惑的魂灵纷纷冲向井口，眼见自己的来世正被夺走，而从井中，我听见了羽翼的声响。一阵冷风自井底涌起，我看见一个身影从井的深处朝我飞升而来。一名女子，双眼上蒙着与我相仿的布，褴褛的束带缠绕在她臂上，织入一袭破烂的裙裳。她生着黝黑的双翼，肌肤苍白如象牙。她宛如透过层层枝叶滤下的月光。[PARAGRAPH:1]可她还不够快。我伸出手，将周围所有的魂灵尽数拉向自己，全部灌注进那道正沿着闭合岩面刻画的最后符文之中。一道屏障牢牢锁定，一面巨大的镜子，会把试图穿越之人尽数送回，一场蜕变，会将穿越它的魂灵缚成不洁之形。[PARAGRAPH:1]魂灵为符文注入了力量，它们被困于其中。它们嚎叫着与符文抗争，却无从逃脱。[PARAGRAPH:1]为了试验这道咒法，我走向近旁一棵苹果树，因鸟儿不敢靠近井口，这般近处的果实无人问津。可时值年初，枝头只挂着一颗颗青涩的小苹果。[PARAGRAPH:1]我在树干上刻下一道枯萎符文，那树立刻萎缩枯死。枝条纤细孱弱之际，那些小苹果纷纷坠落。有那么一瞬什么都没发生，随后那树又重新丰盈起来。它没能长回原来的高度，仍是那咒法所致的黝黑扭曲之态，却也没有彻底死去。它的枝头绽出新的小果，可这一回它们呈深褐红色，缓缓搏动着。[PARAGRAPH:1]我的使命已然开始。我与刻里德温的交易——为造物带来末日决战——由此启程。我若失败，便会重返地狱那永恒的牢狱；而纵然那意味着毁灭世界，我也绝不愿再度承受地狱的折磨。

english: [LINK=UNIT_FAWN]Chapter 1: Beltane Cycle[\\LINK][NEWLINE][LINK=UNIT_SATYR]Chapter 2: Beltane Cycle[\\LINK][NEWLINE][LINK=BUILDING_MONUMENT]Chapter 3: Beltane Cycle[\\LINK][NEWLINE][LINK=BUILDING_MAGE_GUILD]Chapter 4: Beltane Cycle[\\LINK][NEWLINE]Chapter 5: Beltane Cycle[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][TAB]Thessa was only forty summers old when she first laid eyes on Devon. She was sitting on the branches of one of the ancient trees when he came walking along the pathway below. She had heard of him, his mother was said to have been so beautiful that an angel fell in love with her. It was their union that produced Devon, who was talented and graceful even by elven standards.[PARAGRAPH:1]As Thessa leaned further out on the branch to get a closer look, he turned his gaze upwards and looked straight into her eyes. She was so shocked she lost her grip on the branch, and tumbled down into the undergrowth below. She lay there stunned, but she was unsure if this was because of the fall or her embarrassment. A tender hand gripped hers, and she was pulled gently to her feet.[PARAGRAPH:1]"Be careful Parvulus, those branches can be treacherous for the unwary. Especially those who keep their attention... elsewhere." He smiled, and that smile would later be counted among her most treasured memories.[PARAGRAPH:1]Thessa grew to become one of the most powerful mages in Evermore. In her early years she outdid her fellow students in most disciplines, and sometimes she even surpassed her teachers. Once she managed to make an oak grow to its full size overnight from an acorn she had found on the ground, but the exhaustion of that effort left her unconscious for several days.[PARAGRAPH:1]Only one incident served to disturb the teachers' high opinion of her. She was once discovered reading a grimoire of necromancy, a book stolen from the Calabim in earlier times that most of the senior mages had believed to be long since destroyed, or at least locked up safely. The book was immediately confiscated, and it certainly seemed the young girl had not had time to be lured by the forbidden spells. The incident was soon forgotten, as Thessa proved such a brilliant and diligent student.[PARAGRAPH:1]When her formal education came to an end, she was offered the position of archmage, and her strong sense of duty compelled her to accept, even though her most urgent desire was another entirely.[PARAGRAPH:1]At the Beltane festival she and Devon danced all night. Thessa's long black hair, decorated with a single gold feather, flew around her head in time with the elven songs and flute music. The village danced and played beneath the trees and starlight. It was the most brilliant night of her life.[PARAGRAPH:1]Trouble had arrived to the tranquil forest of the elves. Scouts came from the borderlands with horrible tales-not of an intruding enemy army, but of something more sinister. A strange corruption had started to appear. It made grass wither and die, and turned the more sturdy plants into twisted, pus-filled growths which further spread the corruption along with their seeds. Something had to be done before the animals would start dying, and naturally the help of the archmage was sought.[PARAGRAPH:1]Thessa gladly accepted, by then she was so accustomed with her own tremendous power that any task she received seemed easy. Yet the corruption proved too strong for her. Even her most powerful spells of cleansing could only provide momentary relief for a small area, and that at the cost of several days of fatigue. So the corruption was left to roam freely, and it slowly crept towards the center of the forest, and Evermore.[PARAGRAPH:1]Devon wished to marry her. He had made that plain to her at the festival, and she could sense his impatience growing as the days grew by. Finally she gave in, even though she had become preoccupied with thinking of ways to stop the slow degeneration of the woods. Their families started preparations for the grand party, the divine union of the archmage and the aasimar.[PARAGRAPH:1]Meanwhile, Thessa continued to fight her losing battle against the mysterious force at work in the forest. She traveled towards the source of the taint, but could not locate a specific place of origin. It seemed to have appeared in many places simultaneously, and she suspected that some malevolent mage may have cast a powerful spell of entropy on her homeland. On her way back home, she found a clearing where two deer lay dead, their corpses a sickening hue of dark purple. She sat down on the ashen ground in despair, but then she had a sudden, horrible, realization.[PARAGRAPH:1]She grieved for the life that had been lost here, and for the life that would be lost in the near future.[PARAGRAPH:1]The wedding party was truly magnificent. There was a banquet of exotic fruit and excellent wine, there were a large number of skilled musicians, there was singing and dancing. Thessa seemed oddly preoccupied during the event, but most of the guests assumed, as did her fiancée, that it was merely stress from working too hard. As night fell, the guests left the clearing under the great red oak tree, leaving the newlyweds alone at the place of the ceremony to consummate their marriage, in accordance with elvish custom.[PARAGRAPH:1]So they both stood there, Devon's eyes so bright with joy and expectation that Thessa could hardly bear to look at him. Yet she forced herself to smile, and gently drew him closer. Devon was too gripped by the moment to notice the lack of light in her eyes, and the tears that had started to appear there. He tried to kiss her, but she pushed him away, looked into his eyes one last time, and gently whispered:[PARAGRAPH:1]"I am sorry."[PARAGRAPH:1]Before Devon could reply, she drew the ceremonial dagger she had tucked in her dress, and stabbed him in the heart, muttering incomprehensible words of a kind that had not been heard in that forest for hundreds of years. Her spell let her drain the divine spirit out of Devon's body and add it to her own magical power. Filled with such vast energies, she invoked the spell of cleansing. A shockwave emanated from the clearing, flowing through air, earth and trees, and as it swept by, the forest was healed.[PARAGRAPH:1]Morning came. The sun shone brightly on a lush and green forest, teeming with life. All except a body in a clearing, and a weeping woman sitting beside it, her head in her hands.

[LINK=UNIT_FAWN]第一章：贝尔坦轮回[\\LINK][NEWLINE][LINK=UNIT_SATYR]第二章：贝尔坦轮回[\\LINK][NEWLINE][LINK=BUILDING_MONUMENT]第三章：贝尔坦轮回[\\LINK][NEWLINE][LINK=BUILDING_MAGE_GUILD]第四章：贝尔坦轮回[\\LINK][NEWLINE]第五章：贝尔坦轮回[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][TAB]塞莎初次见到德文时，不过四十个夏天的年岁。她正坐在一棵古树的枝桠上，他沿着下方的小径走来。她曾听说过他，据说他母亲美得让一位天使坠入爱河。正是他们的结合诞下了德文，即便以精灵的标准衡量，他也才华横溢、优雅出众。[PARAGRAPH:1]塞莎为了看得更清楚，探身在枝头愈发前倾，他却抬眼向上，直直望进她的眼睛。她惊愕之下失了手，从枝头跌落进下方的灌木丛中。她躺在那里发怔，却分不清是因这一跤，还是因这份窘迫。一只温柔的手握住了她的手，将她轻轻扶起。[PARAGRAPH:1]“当心，小家伙，那些枝桠对粗心之人可是危险的。尤其是那些心思……飘在别处的人。”他微笑着，那笑容后来成了她最珍视的记忆之一。[PARAGRAPH:1]塞莎长成了永恒之城中最强大的法师之一。年少时她在大多数学科上都胜过同窗，有时甚至超越了她的导师。她曾一夜之间用地上拾来的一颗橡实令一棵橡树长至参天之高，可那番耗损令她昏睡了好几天。[PARAGRAPH:1]唯有一桩事曾动摇导师们对她的高度赞许。她曾被发现在研读一本死灵法术的魔典，那是早年从卡拉比姆人手中窃来的书，多数资深法师都以为它早已被销毁，或至少被妥善封存。那书当即被没收，那年幼的女孩看来确实还来不及被禁忌咒法所诱惑。此事很快便被淡忘，因为塞莎证明了自己是何等出众而勤勉的学生。[PARAGRAPH:1]她正式的学业告一段落时，她被授予大法师之职，她强烈的责任感迫使她接受了，尽管她内心最迫切的渴望完全是另一回事。[PARAGRAPH:1]在贝尔坦节庆上，她与德文彻夜起舞。塞莎那头乌黑长发，饰以一根金色羽毛，随着精灵的歌谣与笛声在她头畔飞扬。整座村落在林荫与星光下起舞欢歌。那是她一生中最璀璨的一夜。[PARAGRAPH:1]祸患降临了精灵这片宁静的森林。斥候从边境地带带来了骇人的传闻——不是关于入侵的敌军，而是关于某种更为阴森的东西。一种奇异的腐化开始显现。它令青草枯萎凋亡，将更为坚韧的植物变成扭曲的、脓液淤积的赘生物，这些赘生物又连同它们的种子进一步散播着腐化。必须在走兽开始死亡之前采取对策，大法师的援助自然被请求了。[PARAGRAPH:1]塞莎欣然应允，那时她早已对自己惊人的力量习以为常，任何交派给她的任务都显得轻而易举。可这腐化被证明太过强大。即便是她最强大的净化咒法，也只能为一小片区域带来片刻的缓解，且要以数日的疲乏为代价。于是这腐化被放任肆虐，缓缓蔓延向森林的中心，蔓向永恒之城。[PARAGRAPH:1]德文希望娶她为妻。他在节庆上已把这心意向她挑明，她能感觉到随着时日推移，他的焦切与日俱增。她终于应允了，尽管她已一心扑在如何阻止森林缓慢衰败的思虑上。双方的家族开始筹备那场盛大的婚宴，大法师与天裔的神圣结合。[PARAGRAPH:1]与此同时，塞莎仍在与森林中那股神秘之力打着她那注定败北的仗。她朝着污秽的源头行去，却无法锁定某个具体的源起之地。它似乎同时出现在许多地方，她怀疑是某个恶毒的法师在她的家园施下了一道强大的熵变咒法。归途中，她发现一处林间空地，两头鹿死在那里，它们的尸体泛着令人作呕的暗紫色。她绝望地在那片灰烬般的地上坐下，随后却猛然生出一个突如其来的、可怕的领悟。[PARAGRAPH:1]她为这里逝去的生命哀恸，也为不久将逝去的生命哀恸。[PARAGRAPH:1]那场婚宴当真辉煌无比。有异国的珍果与佳酿的盛宴，有众多技艺娴熟的乐师，有歌，有舞。塞莎在庆典上显得莫名心不在焉，可宾客们大多以为——一如她的未婚夫——那不过是操劳过度的压力所致。夜幕降临，宾客们离开了那棵巨大红橡树下的空地，依照精灵的习俗，把这对新人独自留在婚礼之地圆房。[PARAGRAPH:1]于是二人一同立于那里，德文的双眼因喜悦与期盼而明亮，明亮得让塞莎几乎不忍看他。可她强迫自己微笑，温柔地将他拉近。德文全然沉浸在此刻，未曾留意她眼中缺失的光彩，也未察觉那已在她眼中悄然浮现的泪水。他试图吻她，她却把他推开，最后一次望进他的眼睛，轻声呢喃：[PARAGRAPH:1]“我很抱歉。”[PARAGRAPH:1]德文还未及回应，她便抽出藏在裙中的仪式匕首，刺入了他的心脏，口中念诵着那森林里数百年未曾听闻的、令人费解的言辞。她的咒法让她将德文体内的神圣灵魂抽离，添入自己的魔力之中。充盈着如此浩瀚的能量，她施展了净化的咒法。一道冲击波自空地荡开，穿透空气、大地与林木，所到之处，森林尽皆愈合。[PARAGRAPH:1]清晨来临。阳光明媚地照耀着一片葱郁苍翠、生机盎然的森林。唯一的例外，是空地上的一具尸体，以及坐在它旁边、双手掩面啜泣的女子。

english: [TAB]"Is it done?"[PARAGRAPH:1]Sammuel offered only a painted shell as proof. He wasn't the most talented of Valledia's wizards, but skilled enough in the magic of the mind and soul to do what was required, and particularly unhindered by morals that can conflict with such a task. [PARAGRAPH:1]Valledia nodded and excused the wizard from the chamber, he bowed and slunk out, seeming a jackal to her eyes. But she was no better, her hands were just as bloody for ordering him to the task as he was for completing it. [PARAGRAPH:1]She sat and considered this while she waited for the Caswallawn to arrive. He was ever late, and as undisciplined as he was talented. When finally he arrived he was rushed, as people who cannot keep time always are. [PARAGRAPH:1]"You have released Sammuel from the prisons? He was convicted of unapproved necromancy, of sustaining a creature's life past natural means!" [PARAGRAPH:1]Valledia didn't answer. [PARAGRAPH:1]"He should have been killed for his experimentation, there is no balance in what he was doing, he threatens to incur the wrath of the gods on all of us. First you order him spared, now you let him go. What were you thinking?" [PARAGRAPH:1]"Incur the wrath of the gods?" [PARAGRAPH:1]She knew Dain wasn't religious, he had been listening to the priests ramble on. He started again. [PARAGRAPH:1]"He broke the law, why shouldn't it apply to him? What is special about this man that he should flaunt our restrictions while others are punished justly for them?" [PARAGRAPH:1]"His life is mine to give or take, as is your counsel. Go on to other topics, you won't receive anything that will satisfy you with this one."[PARAGRAPH:1]Dain began to argue back, but he sensed a gravity in her that he didn't understand. She wouldn't be moved on this matter, and Valledia had her reasons even if she wouldn't share them. She was as stubborn and logical a creature as he had ever met. [PARAGRAPH:1]"Fine, to this truce then. The priests say that the Elohim are withdrawing from their war with the Infernals." [PARAGRAPH:1]"And?" [PARAGRAPH:1]"The Infernals are not as weak as some suppose, if they are agreeing to peace with the Elohim then it is only because they wish to carry on battle somewhere else. The Elohim are a powerful force and they must see easier targets to feed upon, the Bannor, the Lanun or us." [PARAGRAPH:1]Valledia waited to see if he would continue with his logic, but for all of his arcane skill he had a disappointing inability to anticipate the future. [PARAGRAPH:1]"The priests are right, at least on this, the Elohim have already agreed to peace. What would you have me do about it?" [PARAGRAPH:1]"We need to go to Cahir Abbey and meet with Einion, to talk him into resuming this war." [PARAGRAPH:1]"Do you think that we could convince Einion to go back on his word? To forfeit a signed deal because if he doesn't sacrifice Elohim lives we might have to sacrifice Amurite ones? Or do you think that even attempting to do that will not only fail but draw the Infernals wrath at our attempt, and we will have the war you fear so much."[PARAGRAPH:1]Dain began pacing. Although shortsighted at times he was an Amurite and once presented with a logical argument he would consider it carefully. He reached out to a burning brazier that hung in the chamber and his finger cut the smoke into twin plumes. At Dain's silent command the smoke gathered and formed itself into two images, one of Hyborem and the other of Einion. He studied both of them, looking for some sign of their nature in the fabricated images. He spoke slowly as he thought through each statement, trying to see if there was anyway to work around it and finding himself trapped by them. [PARAGRAPH:1]"Einion won't break his truce. Hyborem will attack another civilization. If that civilization is us, we will likely die. Do we have something Hyborem wants, something we could trade for peace if we needed it?"[PARAGRAPH:1]"What would a demon want except to kill?" [PARAGRAPH:1]"Is there a reason you suspect that he will attack the Lanun or the Bannor instead of us?" [PARAGRAPH:1]"No, like most predators he will go after the weakest of his targets, that is us. Ready your wizards for war, it will come to us. Slip the firebows from the coastal borders to those we share with the Infernals." [PARAGRAPH:1]Dain nodded, understanding the situation. Understanding that diplomacy was lost, he turned his mind to war. [PARAGRAPH:1]"I will begin to train adepts to sanctify the land, no doubt we will be facing the taint. We may want to consider a show of support for the Order, they could be strong allies soon.” [PARAGRAPH:1]"You are right, I will handle the Order, stay to your mages." [PARAGRAPH:1]"I should go, I have much to do."[PARAGRAPH:1]Valledia nodded and Dain turned to leave. She stopped him before he left the chamber. [PARAGRAPH:1]"Dain, I have foreseen this war and moved to save us from it. Though the night will be long, morning will come. The Elohim will rejoin the war, as they have borne a great enmity against the Infernals and wont be able to watch us fall to them. When the Infernals have taken our border cities and march toward our capitals we will go to them, talk of those we have lost, and they will break their truce and join us." [PARAGRAPH:1]"They bear no love for us. Their hated for the Infernals must be greater than I imagined." [PARAGRAPH:1]Valledia only nodded.
chinese: [TAB]“办妥了吗？”[PARAGRAPH:1]萨缪尔只递上一枚彩绘的贝壳作为凭证。他算不上瓦蕾蒂亚手下最有天赋的术士，可在心灵与魂魄的魔法上足够娴熟，能办成所要之事，尤其不受那些可能与此等任务相抵触的道德所羁绊。[PARAGRAPH:1]瓦蕾蒂亚点点头，示意那术士退出殿堂，他鞠躬后悄然溜走，在她眼中活像一头豺狼。可她并不比他清白，下令让他去办此事，她的双手便与完成此事的他一样沾满了血。[PARAGRAPH:1]她坐着思量此事，等待着卡斯瓦劳恩的到来。他向来迟到，才华有多横溢，就有多散漫无度。他终于到时，形色匆匆，一如所有不守时之人那般。[PARAGRAPH:1]“你把萨缪尔从牢里放出来了？他可是因未经批准的死灵法术、因用违逆自然的手段延续一头生物的性命而被定罪的！”[PARAGRAPH:1]瓦蕾蒂亚没有答话。[PARAGRAPH:1]“他本该因他的试验而被处死，他所做之事毫无平衡可言，他这是要招致诸神对我们所有人降下天谴。你先是下令饶他一命，如今又放他走。你到底在想什么？”[PARAGRAPH:1]“招致诸神的天谴？”[PARAGRAPH:1]她知道丹安并不虔信，他是听那些祭司唠叨多了。他又开口了。[PARAGRAPH:1]“他违了法，凭什么律法就不该管到他头上？这个人有何特别，竟能藐视我们的禁令，而旁人却为同样的事被公正地惩处？”[PARAGRAPH:1]“他的性命由我予夺，一如你的谏言。谈别的吧，这件事上你得不到任何能让你满意的答复。”[PARAGRAPH:1]丹安还想争辩，却感到她身上有一种他所不能理解的凝重。在这件事上她不会被动摇，瓦蕾蒂亚自有她的道理，纵然她不愿说出。她是他所见过最固执、也最讲逻辑的造物。[PARAGRAPH:1]“罢了，那就此休战。祭司们说，埃洛希姆人正从他们与地狱军团的战争中抽身。”[PARAGRAPH:1]“然后呢？”[PARAGRAPH:1]“地狱军团并不像有些人以为的那样弱。他们若肯与埃洛希姆人议和，那只因他们想把战火引往别处。埃洛希姆人是一股强大的力量，他们定是看到了更易攻取的目标——班诺尔、拉努恩，或是我们。”[PARAGRAPH:1]瓦蕾蒂亚等着看他是否会顺着自己的逻辑继续推下去，可尽管他一身秘法造诣，却在预见未来一事上有着令人失望的无能。[PARAGRAPH:1]“祭司们说得对，至少在这一点上——埃洛希姆人已经同意议和了。你要我为此做什么？”[PARAGRAPH:1]“我们得去卡希尔修道院会一会艾尼恩，说服他重启这场战争。”[PARAGRAPH:1]“你以为我们能说动艾尼恩背弃他的誓言？让他毁弃一纸签定的协约，只因倘若他不去牺牲埃洛希姆人的性命，我们或许就得牺牲阿姆莱特人的性命？还是说，你以为这般尝试非但会失败，反倒会因我们的图谋招来地狱军团的怒火，让你我惧怕的那场战争成真？”[PARAGRAPH:1]丹安开始踱步。他虽时而目光短浅，却终究是个阿姆莱特人，一旦有合乎逻辑的论点摆在面前，他便会审慎权衡。他伸手探向殿中悬着的一只燃烧的火盆，指尖将那烟雾切成两道袅袅上升的青烟。在丹安无声的意念驱使下，烟雾聚拢，凝成两幅影像，一幅是海勃雷姆，另一幅是艾尼恩。他端详着二者，试图从这凭空造出的影像中窥见他们本性的某种迹象。他缓缓地开口，一句一句地思量，试图看清有无办法绕开它们，却发现自己被它们困住了。[PARAGRAPH:1]“艾尼恩不会毁弃他的休战。海勃雷姆会去攻打另一个文明。倘若那个文明是我们，我们多半会灭亡。我们可有海勃雷姆想要的东西，某样必要时能用来换取和平的东西？”[PARAGRAPH:1]“除了杀戮，一头恶魔还能想要什么？”[PARAGRAPH:1]“你可有什么缘由，怀疑他会去攻打拉努恩或班诺尔，而非我们？”[PARAGRAPH:1]“没有。像大多数掠食者一样，他会挑目标中最弱的下手，那就是我们。让你的术士们备战吧，战争会找上我们的。把火球射手从沿海的边境调到我们与地狱军团接壤的地方。”[PARAGRAPH:1]丹安点点头，明白了处境。明白外交已然失败，他将心思转向了战争。[PARAGRAPH:1]“我会开始训练术士去圣化土地，无疑我们将要面对那污秽。我们或许该考虑向秩序教团表个态，他们不久或许能成为强大的盟友。”[PARAGRAPH:1]“你说得对，秩序教团我来处理，你只管盯着你的法师。”[PARAGRAPH:1]“我该走了，我还有许多事要办。”[PARAGRAPH:1]瓦蕾蒂亚点点头，丹安转身欲走。她在他离开殿堂前唤住了他。[PARAGRAPH:1]“丹安，我已预见到这场战争，并已着手将我们从中解救。夜虽漫长，晨终将至。埃洛希姆人会重返战场，因为他们对地狱军团怀有莫大的仇怨，绝不会坐视我们败于其手。等地狱军团夺下我们的边境城市、向我们的都城进军之际，我们便去见他们，诉说我们所失去的那些人，他们便会打破休战，加入我们。”[PARAGRAPH:1]“他们对我们并无好感。他们对地狱军团的恨意，想必比我料想的还要深。”[PARAGRAPH:1]瓦蕾蒂亚只是点了点头。

english: [TAB]The Overlord priestess stood quietly on the seashore, her long flowing robe dancing in the storm. She could have done this anywhere on land, but nowhere did it feel as real and invigorating as by the sea, by the storm.[PARAGRAPH:1]"Oh mighty masters, hear my call", she spread out her arms and raised her eyes upwards, towards the storm rising above the sea. "My body and mind are yours to command, my sanity but a tool at your bidding. Honor my sacrifice to you, and grant me the sight of your servant." Intoning the words, she could feel the might that lurked deep below the waves, the ancient and inhuman power. The overwhelming sensation was enough to blind her to the living world and threw her mind into a deep blackness that contained only the ever-stormy nightmares of the Undertow. In the horrible, chaotic maelstrom of bizarre sensations and feelings never meant for mortal eyes, she forced her will, shaped in her head the image of a twisted, many-eyed octopus. As she concentrated on the vision, two of the fish's eyes were torn out of its head in a slimly plop. They stared at the chaos around them and floated in the air, untouched by the raging water and wind.[PARAGRAPH:1]"Your eyes shall be mine", she said in a dry whisper, reached out for the eyes and closed her fist around them. As she felt the large, slimy things against her skin, the storm in her mind quieted and she once again stood on the shore.[PARAGRAPH:2]"And my eyes they will be", she finished, now seeing with two pairs of eyes as she opened her fists to reveal the gifts of her gods. She said nothing more as she lowered her hands and willed the eyes to rise up in the air, go out and spy upon the enemies of the Undertow.
chinese: [TAB]霸主的女祭司静静立于海滨，她那飘曳的长袍在风暴中舞动。她本可在陆上任何地方施行此事，可没有哪里能像在海边、在风暴中这般真切而振奋。[PARAGRAPH:1]“哦，至高的主人们，请听我的呼唤”，她张开双臂，抬眼向上，望向那从海面之上升起的风暴。“我的身与心听凭您差遣，我的神智不过是任您驱使的工具。请受纳我向您的献祭，赐予我一睹您仆从的目力。”她念诵着这些言辞，能感觉到潜伏于波涛深处的伟力，那古老而非人的力量。那压倒性的感受足以令她对生者的世界视而不见，将她的心神抛入一片深邃的黑暗，其中唯有暗流那永不止息的风暴噩梦。在那恐怖、混沌的漩涡里，充斥着从非凡人肉眼所能承受的怪异感受与知觉，她强行运使自己的意志，在脑海中塑出一只扭曲的、生满眼睛的章鱼之形。她凝神于这幻象之际，那鱼头上的两只眼睛随着一声黏滑的“噗”被扯了出来。它们凝视着周遭的混沌，悬浮于空中，不为狂暴的海水与风所动。[PARAGRAPH:1]“你的眼睛将归我所有”，她以干涩的低语说着，伸手去够那两只眼睛，一把攥在掌心。当她感到那两团硕大、黏滑之物抵着她的肌肤时，她心中的风暴平息了，她再度立于海岸之上。[PARAGRAPH:2]“它们也确将成为我的眼睛”，她收尾道，此刻张开双拳，露出她诸神的馈赠，以两对眼睛注视着世界。她不再多言，垂下双手，意念驱使那两只眼睛升入空中，飞出去窥探暗流的敌人。

english: [TAB]It was dusk when the Stonewarden arrived. Few had ever actually seen one in this small village, but I knew his cause full well. The dwarves all made way for him, a few offering cautious greetings, which he ignored. He stopped in a clearing at the other edge of town and surveyed his surroundings, then sat down and began to chant. Soon the earth began to shake, and a cloud of dust surrounded the Stonewarden. The small dwarf children clung tightly to their mothers as the loud scraping of earth and rock echoed through the village. In minutes it was over, and jagged edges of stone began to peak through as the dust settled. Centered where the Stonewarden had sat now stood a Temple of Kilmorph. When the next disciple of the earth mother arrived in this village, they would find a more than receptive group of followers.[PARAGRAPH:2]- recollections of Marost Dzorad, 43rd Treasurer of the Merchants' Guild of Kazak
chinese: [TAB]石守卫抵达时正值黄昏。在这座小村庄里，真正见过石守卫的人寥寥无几，可我对他的使命一清二楚。矮人们纷纷为他让路，几人小心翼翼地打着招呼，却被他置之不理。他在村子另一端的一处空地上停下，环顾四周，随即坐下，开始吟诵。不久，大地便开始震颤，一团尘雾将石守卫团团围住。矮人的孩童们紧紧依偎着母亲，泥土与岩石那响亮的刮擦声回荡在村庄之中。片刻之间一切便告结束，尘埃落定之际，参差嶙峋的石棱开始探出头来。就在石守卫端坐之处的中央，如今矗立起一座基鲁莫夫神庙。当下一位地母的信徒来到这座村庄时，他们将会遇见一群远比想象中更乐于接纳的追随者。[PARAGRAPH:2]——卡扎克商人工会第四十三任司库马罗斯特·佐拉德的回忆

english: [TAB]"My lady... the results of your experiment. Nearly all of them... twisted beyond comprehension..."[PARAGRAPH:1]"Those who weren't cut out for this shouldn't have volunteered," the voice of the priestess was as harsh and merciless as the young man's was quivering. "The ones who perish here wouldn't have survived combat anyway."[PARAGRAPH:1]The men and the women who'd volunteered lay prone on the open field, all covered by monstrous deformities. One seemed to have had all the blood sucked out of him, another man's testicles had grown so huge they had crushed his toes under their weight. The priestess was walking among them, inspecting each before moving on. Clearly, it seemed, one of the ones who wasn't cut out for it was the aide she'd been assigned.[PARAGRAPH:1]"But my lady," he tried one more time, flinching away his gaze from the man whose bowels had exploded rather violently out of his stomach, "There wasn't anything wrong with these troops, that's why you chose them... they would have made excellent soldiers had not..."[PARAGRAPH:1]"And you would make an excellent Drown if you did not shut up," the priestess replied coldly, finally quieting the aide. She stopped in front of one of her test subjects, pausing to take a closer look. The elven woman had been pretty once, but no stretch of the imagination would let you use that word of her anymore. Any fat she might have had was muscle now, and all the muscle she had was grown large enough to stretch and tear away the skin that had once covered it. Her eyes were bulging out of her head, the expanding tissue having forced them out of their sockets-but despite everything, she eyed the priestess with an air of wary satisfaction.[PARAGRAPH:1]"I think this... is exactly what we need," for the first time today, a smile slowly appeared on the priestess's lips. Her eyes glowing, she turned to the aide, joyous laughter in her voice. "I knew the Undertow would not forsake us! They have gifted some of us inhuman strength, enough to take down all of our foes. Find the others who look like this, they're the ones we want."[PARAGRAPH:1]"And... the others?" the man slowly asked.[PARAGRAPH:1]"The others? Oh," the priestess shrugged, having entirely forgotten about the failures already, "I don't think they can be made into Drown anymore, can they? It really doesn't matter, do what you want with them." She turned away from the aide, smiling and looking at the elven woman with love and adoration in her eyes.[PARAGRAPH:1]"You are so pretty that way, my dear. I'm so glad you made it."
chinese: [TAB]“大人……您的试验结果。几乎所有人……都扭曲得难以想象……”[PARAGRAPH:1]“那些不适合此事的人，本就不该自愿前来，”女祭司的嗓音同那年轻人的声音一样，一个冷酷无情，一个颤抖不已。“在这里丧命的那些人，反正也熬不过实战。”[PARAGRAPH:1]那些自愿前来的男男女女俯卧在空旷的原野上，个个满身骇人的畸变。一个像是被吸干了全身的血，另一个男子的睾丸胀得如此巨大，竟把他的脚趾压在了下面。女祭司在他们之间穿行，逐一查看，而后继续前行。显然，那些不适合此事的人当中，有一个正是分派给她的这名副手。[PARAGRAPH:1]“可是大人，”他又试了一次，把目光从那个肠子相当猛烈地从腹中爆出的男子身上撇开，“这些兵卒本没有半点毛病，正因如此您才选中了他们……若非如此，他们本可成为出色的士兵……”[PARAGRAPH:1]“而你若再不闭嘴，倒能成为出色的溺死者，”女祭司冷冷地回道，终于让那副手噤了声。她在自己一名试验对象面前停下，驻足细看。那精灵女子曾经生得标致，可任凭你如何驰骋想象，也再不能用那个词形容她了。她原本或有的脂肪如今尽是肌肉，而她所有的肌肉都膨大到足以将曾经覆盖其上的皮肤撑裂、撕开。她的双眼从头颅中凸出，膨胀的组织已将它们挤出了眼窝——可尽管如此，她仍以一种警惕而满足的神情打量着女祭司。[PARAGRAPH:1]“我想这个……正是我们所需要的，”今日头一回，一丝笑意缓缓浮上女祭司的唇。她双眼放光，转向那副手，嗓音里满是欢欣的笑意。“我就知道暗流不会遗弃我们！他们赐予我们中的一些人非凡人的力量，足以击垮我们所有的敌人。去找出其余长成这样的人，他们才是我们要的。”[PARAGRAPH:1]“那……其余的呢？”那男子缓缓问道。[PARAGRAPH:1]“其余的？哦，”女祭司耸了耸肩，早已把那些失败品忘得一干二净，“我看他们再也变不成溺死者了，是吧？无所谓，随你怎么处置他们。”她转身背对副手，微笑着，以满含爱怜与倾慕的目光注视着那精灵女子。[PARAGRAPH:1]“你那副模样真是美极了，我亲爱的。我真高兴你挺过来了。”

english: Terrim watched in astonishment through his one good eye as the cuts down his legs began to knit themselves together. Small scratches vanished from his arms like shallow puddles evaporating in the sunlight. He felt a distinct tightening in his bowels as the gash across stomach closed. Then a burst of vitality spread through his right hand and, for the first time in several hours, he could feel his fingers. With an unpleasant pop his eyeball returned to it's socket. Sound was coming back to his ears, blurry and indistinct at first, but becoming clearer with each passing second.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"...Thank you, Nerys. Your incantations have been most useful. As always."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]"Any time," replied Nerys, failing to suppress a blush. "You know where to find me."[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Ready to begin once more, the torturer turned back to the rack, salivating, and Terrim's screams echoed around the chamber.
chinese: 特里姆用他那只尚好的眼睛惊愕地注视着，只见他腿上的道道伤口开始自行愈合。手臂上的细小抓痕如阳光下蒸发的浅浅水洼般消失。当腹上的裂口闭合时，他清晰地感到腹中一阵收紧。随后一股生机涌过他的右手，数小时来他头一回能感觉到自己的手指。伴着一声令人不适的“啵”，他的眼球回到了眼窝里。声音正回到他的耳中，起初模糊而含混，却随着每一秒的流逝愈发清晰。[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]“……谢谢你，奈莉丝。你的咒语一如既往地极为管用。”[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]“随时效劳，”奈莉丝答道，没能掩住脸上的红晕。“你知道去哪儿找我。”[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]准备好再度开始，那施刑者垂涎欲滴地转回刑架，特里姆的尖叫再度回荡在密室之中。

chinese: [TAB]“戈恩巴德疼。”[PARAGRAPH:1]“是啊，我知道戈恩巴德疼，看看你，你在外头被揍得可不轻。”[PARAGRAPH:1]“好多兽人打伤戈恩巴德。”[PARAGRAPH:1]“兽人？是吗，那我看见这把插在你肚子里的精工好剑，也是兽人打造的咯？”[PARAGRAPH:1]“戈恩巴德被好多兽人的剑砍了。”[PARAGRAPH:1]“兽人不使……等等。这是什么？这……这是一根鹿角？”[PARAGRAPH:1]“戈恩巴德饿了”[PARAGRAPH:1]“戈恩巴德不会饿，戈恩巴德是个魔像！”[PARAGRAPH:1]“戈恩巴德以为打完仗战士就会饿，所以戈恩巴德吃了”[PARAGRAPH:1]“靠往你喉咙里塞一头鹿？那对你可没好处，也难怪这里头一团糟。”[PARAGRAPH:1]“戈恩巴德抱歉”[PARAGRAPH:1]“你每次擅自脱离队伍就会受损，你必须和其他人待在一起”[PARAGRAPH:1]“戈恩巴德看见兽人，有命令要砸兽人。”[PARAGRAPH:1]“那些是精灵，离他们远点。”[PARAGRAPH:1]“有什么区别？”[PARAGRAPH:1]“问得好。……行吧，除非你和你的部队在一起，否则离一切带尖东西的家伙都远点。”[PARAGRAPH:1]——机械法师艾罗德与铁魔像戈恩巴德在一次修理时的对话。

english: [TAB]In a graveyard the deceased appear as they wished to be, and not as they actually were. A stone inscribed, "Maria Ghouls, devoted wife of Paulus and loving mother of Henri" ignores the years of fights and beatings at her husband's hand, beatings that eventually led to her death. It doesn't tell of the abuse the father turned on his son after Maria died.[PARAGRAPH:1]They are even worse when the stone mason doesn't know what really happened. Beside her grave another stone reads, "Paulus Ghouls, unable to live without his beloved wife". The stone mason suspected sorrow caused Paulus to walk to the city square and slit his own throat with a quill knife. The mason didn't know that after another night of beating his 10 year old son the boy manifested latent magical powers. The boy used those powers to dominate his father and force him to march out to the city square and kill himself.[PARAGRAPH:1]The tragedy's of a few decades are refined in the graveyard. Though the truth of our lives is too quickly forgotten, our lies are preserved in stone for centuries.
chinese: [TAB]在墓地里，逝者呈现出他们所希望的模样，而非他们实际的模样。一块刻着“玛丽亚·古尔斯，保卢斯挚爱的妻子、亨利慈爱的母亲”的墓碑，无视了她丈夫经年累月的殴打与虐待，正是那些殴打最终要了她的命。它也只字不提玛丽亚死后，那父亲转而施加在儿子身上的虐待。[PARAGRAPH:1]当石匠不知晓真相时，这些墓碑更是不堪。在她的墓旁，另一块石碑刻着“保卢斯·古尔斯，痛失挚爱之妻，无以为继”。石匠猜想是悲痛驱使保卢斯走到城中广场，用一柄削羽刀割断了自己的喉咙。石匠不知道的是，在又一夜殴打他十岁的儿子之后，那男孩显露出了潜藏的魔法之力。男孩用那力量支配了他的父亲，逼他行至城中广场自尽。[PARAGRAPH:1]数十载的悲剧在墓地里被精炼提纯。尽管我们生平的真相太快被人遗忘，我们的谎言却被镌刻在石头里，保存数百年。

english: [TAB]From his position on the turret, Garim watched the Hippus muster on the horizon knowing that they were building for yet another assault. The Khazad had withstood five days of siege from those that would sack the vaults they had worked hard to build.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]He appeared stone-faced, but to those that knew him the evidence of concern was in his eyes. The Hippus numbers had steadily grown day by day whilst the Khazad strength had steadily jaded. They had defended stoutly, and extracted a heavy price of the Hippus-but Rhoanna knew the value of the mines in these hills.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]There...movement on the horizon. A change in the atmosphere-dirty black clouds polluting the once bright daylight. The call to arms. Garim felt satisfaction that the call was not met by cries anguish, but by sturdy acceptance that each shall do their utmost. But still this time there was that unsettling feeling that the toil of his kin would be lost to these plunderers.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]As he adjusted his armor, and tightened the grip on his battle hammer he noted the appearance of the Stonewarden, his heavy soul lifted just at the sight. The Stonewarden addressed his unit, and in an earthy growl repeated three words[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Honesty[NEWLINE]Endeavour[NEWLINE]Tradition[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]and Garim knew, that he and his brethren would stand strong.
chinese: [TAB]从他在塔楼上的位置，加林注视着希普斯人在地平线上集结，深知他们正在为又一次强攻蓄势。卡扎德人已经顶住了那些企图洗劫他们辛苦筑就的宝库之人长达五日的围攻。[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]他神色如铁，可在了解他的人眼中，忧虑的迹象尽在他的眼里。希普斯人的数量日复一日地稳步增长，而卡扎德人的力量却在日渐衰竭。他们坚定地防守，令希普斯人付出了惨重的代价——可罗安娜深知这些山中矿藏的价值。[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]那里……地平线上有了动静。空气中起了变化——污浊的黑云玷污了原本明亮的天光。这是号令备战之声。加林感到欣慰，那号令换来的不是苦痛的哀嚎，而是坚毅的领受，人人皆将竭尽全力。可这一回，仍有那令人不安的感觉：他族人的辛劳恐将断送于这些掠夺者之手。[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]当他整了整甲胄、握紧手中的战锤时，他注意到石守卫的现身，仅是这一眼，便令他沉重的心为之一振。石守卫向他的队伍训话，以一种泥土般低沉的嗓音重复着三个词[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]诚实[NEWLINE]奋进[NEWLINE]传统[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]加林由此知晓，他与他的弟兄们将坚不可摧。

english: [TAB]The Kraken's swimming was slow, leisurely. Thoughts took a while to cross from one edge of its immense brain to the other, the movements of its tentacles almost independent of its mind. Somewhere, far away on the surface, it could faintly sense a distant call which it couldn't resist. But it was not yet in any rush, instinctively knowing that the caller would need time to prepare.[PARAGRAPH:1]In a lazy motion, one of its tentacles made a slow wave around it, dozens of the small fish surrounding it getting caught in the suction cups. It brought the tentacle back to one of its mouths, dined on its snack. A huge swarm of fish followed it wherever it went-countless of them would end up as its meal, but even more would get to dine on its bigger catches. The swarm stretched back for tens of miles, twice as far as the Kraken itself.[PARAGRAPH:1]Gradually it started getting closer to the surface, could feel the call growing more and more demanding. The fish dispersed in fright and then reassembled as the Kraken began swimming faster, faster than it usually ever did. The alien presence was now a burning sun buried in its brain, no longer willing to tolerate any delay. For all of its size, dwarfing small islands, the Kraken was only a servant for the true lords of the sea.[PARAGRAPH:1]When the chosen of the Undertow called, it would obey and serve with all its might.
chinese: [TAB]大海妖游得缓慢而悠然。念头要从它那庞大脑袋的一端传到另一端，得费上好一阵子，它触手的动作几乎独立于它的心智之外。在遥远的某处，在海面之上，它能隐隐感到一声无法抗拒的遥远召唤。可它尚不着急，本能地知道那召唤者需要时间准备。[PARAGRAPH:1]它慵懒地摆动，一条触手在身周缓缓一挥，围绕它的数十条小鱼被吸盘困住。它把触手收回一张口中，享用起这份小食。一大群鱼追随着它，无论它去往何处——其中数不清的鱼终将成为它的一餐，可更多的鱼却能靠它更大的猎物果腹。这鱼群向后绵延数十英里，长度是大海妖本身的两倍。[PARAGRAPH:1]它渐渐开始靠近海面，能感到那召唤愈发迫切。鱼群受惊四散，又在大海妖开始加速游动时重新聚拢，它游得比往常任何时候都快。那异己的存在此刻已如一轮燃烧的烈日，深埋于它的脑中，再不肯容忍半分拖延。尽管体型硕大，堪比小岛，大海妖也不过是海洋真正主人的仆从。[PARAGRAPH:1]当暗流的选民召唤时，它便会服从，倾尽全力效命。

english: [TAB]The Trust Glamour is a strange one, inasmuch as it reveals far more about those that deal with the one enchanted than the enchanted themselves. The Khazad see a prosperous merchant, noble and sound in all his business dealings. The Lanun and Grigori see valiant heroes, wandering the world with a Agares-may-care swagger. For the Doviello, a magnificent warrior, fresh from the field of battle. With the Sheaim, the glamour amplifies paranoia, causing mistrust in everyone save the target. Strangest of all is the Infernal reaction. Despite seeing through the deception, the demons cannot help but admire the cynicism of anyone who would resort to such a spell.
